Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
27-year-old male with 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhoea, crampy mid-lower abdominal pain, mild vomiting, and subjective fever; clinical picture most consistent with acute infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral).

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden onset profuse watery diarrhoea starting ~3 days ago; stool frequency ~hourly while awake.  
• Associated symptoms: Colicky mid-lower abdominal cramps (6/10, precede stools), nausea, occasional vomiting (worse with milk), feels febrile (“burning up”), slightly reduced urine output. No blood in stool.  
• Pertinent negatives: No mucus, no constant severe pain, no weight loss, no recent travel, no regular medications causing diarrhoea.  
• Past medical history: Denies chronic illnesses; otherwise fit and well.  
• Medications: Intermittent paracetamol for pain/fever; no regular Rx.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Family history: Father with stage III colon cancer; brother currently has similar diarrhoeal illness ×5 days.  
• Social / preventive: Lives with mother & sister; office worker (government). Social smoker; alcohol socially/binge monthly. Often eats takeaway. No recent temperature measurement; no vaccinations discussed.

Examination:
Tele-consultation—no objective vitals available. Patient appears well enough to converse; subjectively febrile. No other physical findings provided.

Impression:
Most likely:  
1. Acute viral gastroenteritis (high likelihood) — abrupt onset, watery stool, household contact with identical illness, mild systemic symptoms.  
2. Acute bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis (medium likelihood) — takeaway food habit and subjective fever; less likely given absence of blood/mucus.  
Less likely contributors: transient post-infectious lactose intolerance (milk triggers vomiting), early inflammatory bowel disease (acute presentation and lack of blood make this unlikely).

Plan:
• Hydration: Encourage copious clear fluids; start oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte; OTC).  
• Diet: Light soft diet (soups, mashed foods) as tolerated; gradually re-introduce solids. Avoid dairy until recovery; avoid alcohol.  
• Symptom control: Continue paracetamol for fever/abdominal discomfort within recommended dosing.  
• Warning / follow-up: If diarrhoea or vomiting persist >48 hours, worsen, or signs of dehydration (tachycardia, dizziness, minimal urine), contact clinic urgently for in-person review, vitals, and possible labs/stool cultures.  
• No antibiotics prescribed at this stage; expect self-limiting course.  
• Safety net: Seek immediate care for blood in stool, persistent high fever, severe abdominal pain, or inability to keep fluids down.

Quality checks
● Missing but expected: Objective vitals (temperature, HR, BP), weight change, travel/food exposure details, stool frequency count per 24 h, immunization status, workplace/public health advice, formal dehydration assessment.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Tele-visit with fair audio; no physical exam possible; some conversational interruptions but history broadly complete.
